cognate: Armenian anun and Vedic nāman continue *h₁nómn̥; Armenian dnem/edeal and Vedic dhā continue *dʰeh₁-. Greek onoma with tithēmi independently preserves the same combination.
drift_or_renewal: none in the lexical pair; place naming in Armenian, divine naming in Vedic, personal naming in Homer.
shared_syntax: Name is the theme of put/set: active participial naming in Armenian and passive establishment of the name in Vedic. Greek active/middle naming supports the construction.
context: The Armenian narrator explains a place-name assigned after boundary construction; the Vedic hymn declares the name Agni established. Both concern assignment of a designation, not mere juxtaposition of name and an unrelated act of placing. The nonliteral choice of set for naming, with the same inherited noun and verb in three traditions, favors a traditional collocation over random root overlap. Its productivity and the late Armenian witness keep confidence below high.
phrase: *h₁nómn̥ dʰeh₁-: set a name, name something.

search_lead.slab_anchor: xcl:MH_1_2_11_Agathangelos ed. page 1365 - PDF page 71 (word id 12638) (w3/3)
search_lead.cognate: Armenian tesanem and Greek derkomai continue *derḱ-. Armenian loys and Greek phaos are not cognate: the light noun is renewed.
search_lead.argument: Armenian keal and zloys tesanel coordinates living with seeing light; the Greek alternatives dead or seeing light make the same life/death metonym explicit. This is stronger than the retrieved Latin syntactic parallels, but Greek influence on Armenian Christian prose and the general naturalness of the metaphor must be assessed before asserting inheritance.
